1	# DevDesk Backlog
2	
3	**Last Updated:** 2026-08-01
4	
5	Open work for DevDesk: known defects, technical debt, and planned features.
6	Replaces the former `todo.md` at the repository root. Items completed there
7	(network topology visualisation, inter-container ping/curl) have been dropped
8	rather than carried over.
9	
10	---
11	
12	## 1. Known defects
13	
14	None of these are fixed. Each is reachable from the current code unless noted.
15	
16	### D1 — `ReportModal.View()` emits invalid UTF-8
17	
18	`internal/ui/components/report_modal.go:136-139`
19	
20	Long entries are truncated with `item[len(item)-52:]`, which slices **bytes**, not
21	runes. When the resulting offset falls inside a multi-byte codepoint the rendered
22	output is no longer valid UTF-8 and the terminal shows replacement characters.
23	
24	Reachable with any non-ASCII repository path. Pinned by
25	`TestReportModalViewTruncationSplitsMultibyteRunes`, which `t.Skip()`s with
26	instructions once the truncation becomes rune-aware.
27	
28	**Fix:** truncate on `[]rune`, and measure width with `runewidth` rather than
29	`len()`.
30	
31	### D2 — The "permanent delete" checkbox is documented as locked but is not
32	
33	`internal/ui/components/delete_confirm_modal.go:35` and `:99-105`
34	
35	`NewDeleteConfirmModalPermanent` pre-checks *Immediate deletion* and its doc
36	comment states the box is non-modifiable ("pré-cochée et non modifiable"). Nothing
37	enforces that: `space` and `enter` on the checkbox still toggle it.
38	
39	A project already marked for deletion can therefore be sent through a
40	grace-period delete that the caller does not expect. Pinned by
41	`TestDeleteConfirmModalPermanentCheckboxIsStillToggleable`.
42	
43	**Fix:** carry a `locked` flag on the modal and make the toggle a no-op when set,
44	or drop the claim from the doc comment.
45	
46	### D3 — `wrapInputLines` loops forever when `wrapWidth <= 0`
47	
48	`internal/ui/components/wrapped_input.go:135`
49	
50	With a non-positive wrap width the loop makes no progress: `breakAt` collapses to
51	`start`, an empty line is appended, and `start` never advances — the line slice
52	grows until the process runs out of memory.
53	
54	**Not reachable today.** Every caller passes 60, 80 or 100 per Rule 133. Latent
55	only, which is why no test covers it (the test would hang).
56	
57	**Fix:** guard the entry point — return a single line when `wrapWidth < 1`.
58	
59	### D4 — `DeleteConfirmModal` uses `Tab` for field navigation
60	
61	`internal/ui/components/delete_confirm_modal.go:89-97`
62	
63	`tab` / `shift+tab` cycle checkbox → Yes → No. Rule 135 reserves those keys for
64	tab switching and assigns field navigation to `↑ / ↓` exclusively.
65	
66	Cosmetic in isolation, but it is the kind of inconsistency Rule 135 exists to
67	prevent. Changing it alters muscle memory, so it needs a deliberate call rather
68	than a drive-by fix.
69	
70	### D5 — Unreachable focus clamp in `CreationForm`
71	
72	`internal/ui/components/creation_form.go:221-223`
73	
74	After cycling the resource type, the code clamps `focusedField` down to
75	`maxField()`. The surrounding branch only runs when `focusedField == 0`, and
76	`maxField()` is never below 4, so the clamp can never fire.
77	
78	Dead defensive code. Harmless, but it implies a state transition that cannot
79	happen and is misleading to read.
80	
81	### D6 — `wordWrap` measures bytes, not runes
82	
83	`internal/ui/help/help.go:123`
84	
85	Word widths come from `len(word)`, which counts bytes. Accented text therefore
86	wraps earlier than its rendered width requires: two 5-rune words occupy 11
87	columns but 21 bytes, so a width of 12 splits them apart.
88	
89	Low impact today — Rule 129 keeps help content in English US — but it is the same
90	byte-vs-rune class as [D1](#d1--reportmodalview-emits-invalid-utf-8). Unlike
91	[D3](#d3--wrapinputlines-loops-forever-when-wrapwidth--0), `wordWrap` does guard
92	a non-positive width, and that guard is covered by a test so it does not get
93	"tidied" away.
94	
95	Pinned by `TestWordWrapMeasuresBytesNotRunes`.
96	
97	**Fix:** measure with `utf8.RuneCountInString`, or `runewidth.StringWidth` if
98	double-width glyphs ever appear.
99	
100	### D7 — `extractTarGz` keeps parent references in archive paths
101	
102	`internal/oci/oci.go:262`
103	
104	Extraction strips leading `./` and `/` but does not reject `..`, so an archive
105	member named `../../etc/passwd` survives as a map key containing parent
106	references.
107	
108	**Not exploitable today.** The sole consumer, `applyTemplate` in
109	`internal/ui/gitlab/explorer/model.go:1053`, turns the map into GitLab commit
110	actions rather than writing to disk, and the server validates the paths.
111	
112	Recorded because the hazard is latent: any future caller that writes these keys
113	under a target directory inherits a Zip Slip. Pinned by
114	`TestExtractTarGzPreservesParentTraversalInKeys`.
115	
116	**Fix:** reject entries whose cleaned path escapes the root, before returning
117	them.
118	
119	---
120	
121	## 2. Technical debt
122	
123	### Test coverage
124	
125	Currently **13.6 %** overall; the agreed target is 80 %, which needs roughly
126	**+7 700 covered statements** over today's ~1 570.
127	
128	Phased plan, with the harness and most of phase 1 delivered:
129	
130	| Phase | Scope | Status |
131	|---|---|---|
132	| 0 | `internal/ui/testutil` Bubble Tea harness | **done** (100 %) |
133	| 1 | Leaf components and pure helpers | **mostly done** — see the table below; `credentials`, `gitlab` and the `ui/theme` complement remain (~255 stmts) |
134	| 2 | Mid-size view state machines (`status`, `containers`, `dashboard`, `gitlab/auth`) | pending (~1 240 stmts) |
135	| 3 | Large views (`workspaces`, `explorer`, `security`, `netdiag`) | pending (~2 470 stmts) |
136	| 4 | `ui/oci_resources` | pending (~1 995 stmts) |
137	| 5 | Router and I/O seams (`app`, `scan`, `docker`) | pending (~1 360 stmts) |
138	| 6 | Remainder to reach 80 % | pending (~400 stmts) |
139	
140	Phase 1 progress:
141	
142	| Package | Before | Now |
143	|---|---|---|
144	| `internal/ui/testutil` | — | **100 %** (new) |
145	| `internal/ui/shortcut` | 0 % | **100 %** |
146	| `internal/ui/help` | 0 % | **96.7 %** |
147	| `internal/ui/components` | 0 % | **79.8 %** |
148	| `internal/oci` | 0 % | **33.6 %** |
149	| `internal/credentials` | 29.5 % | unchanged |
150	| `internal/gitlab` | 7.5 % | unchanged |
151	
152	`internal/oci` stops at 33.6 % because the remaining statements are registry HTTP
153	paths (`DownloadTemplate`, `listCatalog`, `ListTemplates`) that need a fuller
154	`httptest` fixture — a manifest plus a gzipped layer — rather than the
155	single-response stubs used so far.
156	
157	Phase 5 requires a refactor before it can start: `internal/docker/client.go`
158	shells out to the Docker CLI directly, so it needs an injectable execution seam
159	to be testable.
160	
161	### Files over the 800-line ceiling
162	
163	The project's own coding rules cap files at 800 lines. Eight exceed it:
164	
165	| File | Lines |
166	|---|---|
167	| `internal/ui/security/model.go` | 1785 |
168	| `internal/ui/oci_resources/update.go` | 1556 |
169	| `internal/app/app.go` | 1333 |
170	| `internal/ui/gitlab/explorer/model.go` | 1214 |
171	| `internal/ui/workspaces/model.go` | 1133 |
172	| `internal/docker/client.go` | 1069 |
173	| `internal/ui/netdiag/model.go` | 995 |
174	| `internal/ui/oci_resources/registry_browser.go` | 822 |
175	
176	This interacts with the coverage work: writing several thousand statements of
177	tests against these files before splitting them freezes their current structure.
178	Decide the order deliberately.
179	
180	### Race detector cannot run locally
181	
182	`mise run test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler on `PATH`. Without one
183	it fails with `cgo: C compiler "gcc" not found`. Bubble Tea `Cmd`s run
184	concurrently, so this is the check most likely to catch a Rule 110 violation —
185	it should run in CI even if local machines lack a toolchain.
186	
187	---
188	
189	## 3. Planned features
190	
191	Carried over from `todo.md`.
192	
193	### 3.1 Network diagnostics
194	
195	- **Port-forwarding manager** — an interactive dashboard to manage port
196	  redirections to the host machine.
197	
198	### 3.2 Interactive security remediation
199	
200	- **Auto-patch assistance** — after a Trivy scan, offer to generate a patch or an
201	  updated `Dockerfile` that bumps the base image version to clear critical CVEs.
202	- **Local SAST** — wire security linters (Gitleaks for secrets, IaC linters)
203	  directly into the Workspace view.
204	
205	### 3.3 OCI build and cache analyser
206	
207	- **Layer visualisation** — analyse a local image and show the size of each
208	  layer, in the spirit of `dive`. Intended approach:
209	  - Integrated via `google/go-containerregistry` ("daemonless", no dependency on
210	    the Docker daemon).
211	  - Talk to OCI registries directly, pulling manifests and configs without
212	    downloading the whole image.
213	  - Stream layers in memory (`tar`) to rebuild the filesystem tree.
214	  - Compute wasted space by detecting whiteout files (`.wh.`).
215	- **Cache-miss analysis** — explain why a build's cache was invalidated, e.g.
216	  "`package.json` changed, invalidating the cache".
217	
218	### 3.4 Spontaneous dev containers
219	
220	- **Configuration injection** — inject the developer's dotfiles (vim, zsh,
221	  aliases) when opening a terminal inside a container.
222	- **Hot volume mount** — mount the current working directory into a running
223	  container on the fly, to test a local script without rebuilding the image.
224	
225	### 3.5 Resource dashboard (embedded mini-htop)
226	
227	- **TUI charts** — braille-character charts showing live CPU, RAM and network I/O
228	  for every container in the selected project.
229	- **Visual alerts** — user-defined thresholds (e.g. memory saturation).
230	
231	---
232	
233	## 4. Existing plans
234	
235	Detailed plans live in `.claude/plans/`. One is referenced directly from the old
236	`todo.md` and is still outstanding:
237	
238	- [`platform_compatibility_improvements.md`](../.claude/plans/platform_compatibility_improvements.md)
239	  — Docker-layer platform portability.

content.text:
Le backlog est à jour (`docs/backlog.md`, rien de nouveau depuis le rename du module en #4). J'ai vérifié la couverture réelle — elle correspond aux chiffres du doc.

## La suite immédiate : finir la phase 1 de la couverture

C'est la seule ligne du backlog explicitement « en cours ». Restent trois packages (~255 statements) :

| Package | Actuel | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `internal/gitlab` | **7.5 %** | le plus gros gain ; client API, à tester via `httptest` |
| `internal/credentials` | **29.5 %** | `FileStorage` / `MemoryStorage` testables directement, `GitCredentialStorage` demande un seam d'exec |
| `internal/ui/theme` | **78.9 %** | complément (helpers `Bg`/`PadWithBg`/`TimeAgo`, `TableStylesFor*`) |

Un package n'apparaît dans aucune phase du plan : **`internal/registrymgr` à 18.5 %**. Oubli à corriger dans le tableau.

## Ensuite, un arbitrage à trancher avant la phase 2

Le backlog le signale mais ne le résout pas : les vues de la phase 2/3 (`security/model.go` 1785 lignes, `oci_resources/update.go` 1556, `app.go` 1333…) dépassent le plafond de 800 lignes. Écrire quelques milliers de statements de tests contre elles **fige leur structure actuelle**. Deux ordres possibles :

1. **Découper d'abord** — plus lent à démarrer, mais les tests écrits ensuite restent valides.
2. **Tester d'abord** — filet de sécurité pour le découpage, mais tests à réécrire après.

Mon avis : découper d'abord `internal/docker/client.go`, parce qu'il est de toute façon bloquant — la phase 5 ne peut pas commencer sans un seam d'exécution injectable (il `exec` le CLI Docker en direct). Ce refactor sert deux objectifs à la fois.

## Défauts : les moins chers d'abord

**D1** (`ReportModal` tronque sur les octets → UTF-8 invalide) et **D6** (`wordWrap` mesure des octets) sont la même classe de bug, tous deux épinglés par des tests en `t.Skip()`, tous deux corrigeables en quelques lignes avec `runewidth`. **D3** (boucle infinie si `wrapWidth <= 0`) est un garde d'une ligne. Les trois tiennent dans une seule PR.

**D2** et **D4** demandent une décision de ta part, pas du code : D2 = soit verrouiller la checkbox, soit retirer l'affirmation du commentaire ; D4 = changer `Tab` en `↑/↓` casse la mémoire musculaire.

Par quoi je commence — la phase 1, le refactor `docker/client.go`, ou le lot de défauts UTF-8 ?
corrige le lot de défaut UTF-8, ensuite découpe
Je commence par le lot UTF-8 (D1, D6, D3), puis j'enchaîne sur le découpage.

1	package components
2	
3	import (
4		"fmt"
5		"strings"
6	
7		tea "github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea"
8		"github.com/charmbracelet/lipgloss"
9	
10		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/theme"
11	)
12	
13	// PullReport contains the results of a recursive pull operation
14	type PullReport struct {
15		Cloned  []string
16		Skipped []string
17		Errors  []string
18	}
19	
20	// ReportModal displays the results of an operation
21	type ReportModal struct {
22		title        string
23		report       PullReport
24		scrollOffset int
25		maxVisible   int
26		activeTab    int // 0 = Cloned, 1 = Skipped, 2 = Errors
27		width        int
28		height       int
29	}
30	
31	// NewReportModal creates a new report modal
32	func NewReportModal(title string, report PullReport) *ReportModal {
33		return &ReportModal{
34			title:        title,
35			report:       report,
36			scrollOffset: 0,
37			maxVisible:   10,
38			activeTab:    0,
39		}
40	}
41	
42	// ReportModalCloseMsg is sent when the modal is closed
43	type ReportModalCloseMsg struct{}
44	
45	// Update handles messages
46	func (m *ReportModal) Update(msg tea.Msg) (*ReportModal, tea.Cmd) {
47		switch msg := msg.(type) {
48		case tea.WindowSizeMsg:
49			m.width = msg.Width
50			m.height = msg.Height
51	
52		case tea.KeyMsg:
53			switch msg.String() {
54			case "tab", "right", "l":
55				// Switch tab
56				m.activeTab = (m.activeTab + 1) % 3
57				m.scrollOffset = 0
58	
59			case "shift+tab", "left", "h":
60				// Switch tab backwards
61				m.activeTab = (m.activeTab + 2) % 3
62				m.scrollOffset = 0
63	
64			case "up", "k":
65				if m.scrollOffset > 0 {
66					m.scrollOffset--
67				}
68	
69			case "down", "j":
70				currentList := m.getCurrentList()
71				if m.scrollOffset < len(currentList)-m.maxVisible {
72					m.scrollOffset++
73				}
74	
75			case "enter", "esc", "q":
76				return m, func() tea.Msg {
77					return ReportModalCloseMsg{}
78				}
79			}
80		}
81	
82		return m, nil
83	}
84	
85	// getCurrentList returns the currently active list
86	func (m *ReportModal) getCurrentList() []string {
87		switch m.activeTab {
88		case 0:
89			return m.report.Cloned
90		case 1:
91			return m.report.Skipped
92		case 2:
93			return m.report.Errors
94		default:
95			return []string{}
96		}
97	}
98	
99	// View renders the modal
100	func (m *ReportModal) View() string {
101		var b strings.Builder
102	
103		// Title
104		b.WriteString(theme.TitleStyle.Render(m.title))
105		b.WriteString("\n\n")
106	
107		// Summary
108		summary := fmt.Sprintf("✓ %d cloned  •  ⊘ %d skipped  •  ✗ %d errors",
109			len(m.report.Cloned),
110			len(m.report.Skipped),
111			len(m.report.Errors),
112		)
113		summaryStyle := lipgloss.NewStyle().Background(theme.ColorBackground).Bold(true)
114		b.WriteString(summaryStyle.Render(summary))
115		b.WriteString("\n\n")
116	
117		// Tabs
118		tabs := m.renderTabs()
119		b.WriteString(tabs)
120		b.WriteString("\n\n")
121	
122		// Current list content
123		currentList := m.getCurrentList()
124		if len(currentList) == 0 {
125			emptyMsg := theme.DimStyle.Render("(empty)")
126			b.WriteString(emptyMsg)
127		} else {
128			// Render visible items
129			endIdx := m.scrollOffset + m.maxVisible
130			if endIdx > len(currentList) {
131				endIdx = len(currentList)
132			}
133	
134			for i := m.scrollOffset; i < endIdx; i++ {
135				item := currentList[i]
136				// Truncate long paths
137				if len(item) > 55 {
138					item = "..." + item[len(item)-52:]
139				}
140				b.WriteString("  • " + item + "\n")
141			}
142	
143			// Scroll indicator
144			if len(currentList) > m.maxVisible {

### 1.1 Fixed

**D1** (`ReportModal.View()` emitted invalid UTF-8), **D3** (`wrapInputLines`
looped forever when `wrapWidth <= 0`) and **D6** (`wordWrap` measured bytes) were
fixed together, since D1 and D6 were the same byte-vs-rune defect.

Rather than patch each call site, the truncation logic moved into
`internal/ui/theme/text.go` per Rule 117: `StringWidth`, `TruncateWidth` (keeps
the head) and `TruncateTailWidth` (keeps the tail, for paths). All three measure
terminal columns, so double-width glyphs are handled too, not just multibyte
ones.

A **fourth site carried the same defect** and was not recorded here: `truncate`
in `internal/ui/security/model.go` sliced bytes exactly like D1 and rendered
Trivy finding titles. It is now `theme.TruncateWidth` and the local helper is
gone.

The two pinned tests that `t.Skip()`d became real assertions
(`TestReportModalViewKeepsMultibyteRunesIntact`,
`TestWordWrapMeasuresColumnsNotBytes`).

One call site was deliberately left alone: `truncateResultLine` in
`internal/ui/oci_resources/connectivity_form.go` counts runes rather than bytes,
so it is correct — merely imprecise on double-width glyphs. Folding it into the
theme helpers is a cleanup, not a defect fix.

fix: measure text in columns, not bytes, when truncating and wrapping

Fixes the byte-vs-rune defect lot from docs/backlog.md — D1, D3 and D6 — plus a
fourth site the backlog did not record.

D1: ReportModal.View() truncated long entries with item[len(item)-52:], slicing
bytes. Any non-ASCII repository path could put that offset inside a codepoint,
after which the whole modal rendered as replacement characters.

D6: help.wordWrap took word widths from len(word), so accented text wrapped a
rune early — two 5-column words measure 21 bytes and split at width 12.

D1 and D6 are the same defect, so the logic moved into a shared helper rather
than being patched twice (Rule 117): internal/ui/theme/text.go now exports
StringWidth, TruncateWidth (keeps the head, for titles and messages) and
TruncateTailWidth (keeps the tail, for paths, where the trailing segments are
what identify the item). All three measure terminal columns rather than runes,
so a CJK glyph counts as the 2 columns it occupies; TruncateTailWidth stops
before a glyph that would overflow instead of splitting it.

The fourth site: truncate() in internal/ui/security/model.go sliced bytes
exactly like D1 and rendered Trivy finding titles, which are arbitrary upstream
text. Now theme.TruncateWidth; the local helper is deleted. The titleWidth-3
argument at the call site is left as-is — the helper reserves room for the
marker itself, so passing a pre-reduced width only shortens the title slightly,
and changing it would shift the column layout.

D3: wrapInputLines looped forever on a non-positive wrap width — the break point
collapsed onto start, an empty line was appended and start never advanced, so
the slice grew until the process died. Not reachable today (Rule 133 fixes every
caller at 60/80/100), so the guard refuses to wrap rather than inventing a
fallback width, and the test asserts termination.

TruncateWidth needed a guard of its own: runewidth.Truncate never shortens its
tail marker, so a budget below 3 columns came back wider than requested. Caught
by asserting the column budget across the whole table, not just the golden
strings.

The two pinned tests that t.Skip()d are now real assertions.
